sprint: Magic Card Home — Redesigned Hero Layout, Largest Front/Back Yet
task: Direct follow-up on the immediately-prior card-size sprint, once the user actually saw Magic Card Home rendered with the newly-generalized clamp(150px,32vw,240px) size: 'give me a better screen for this. largest possible size for front and back.' A genuine layout redesign, not just a bigger number in one place -- reclaimed real vertical/horizontal room across the whole screen so the card itself could grow well past that shared 240px ceiling (Home is the one screen whose entire purpose is showing this card, unlike the ceremony's First Claimed Moment or the nickname-prompt preview, each one beat inside a longer flow -- both deliberately untouched, still the shared, more modest size). Restructured openHome()'s DOM: the nickname/since block, which used to sit stacked BELOW the card as its own two lines of vertical footprint, now shares one thin header row with the back button instead (back on the left, name+since right-aligned on the right, new .magic-card-home-header/-identity), directly funding a bigger hero row. Widened the whole panel (.magic-card-home-panel and its ancestor #magicCardContent/.magic-card-panel, kept in lockstep exactly like the prior sprint's own gate-mode override) from 600px to min(94vw,1040px) so a genuinely large Front/Back pair has real room to sit side by side without wrapping. The new .magic-card-home-panel .magic-card-art-canvas rule -- max(90px, min(30vw,380px,calc((100vh-420px)*0.7143))) -- ties sizing to this screen's own real measured footprint (420px, derived from its base-size header/reveal-note/action-buttons/stories-strip/padding) rather than a guessed flat number, so a typical viewport binds on the height term and a tall one on the flat 380px ceiling (kept comfortably under the canvas's own native 700px resolution, so always downscaled, never blurry); the max(90px,...) floor matches _fitAwakenStageToAvailableSpace's own established floor so nothing renders invalid before that function's real, dynamic shrink-to-fit safety net (completely unchanged) gets a chance to run on anything shorter. Also condensed the stories row from an up-to-2-row CSS grid into a fixed-height horizontal scroll strip (fixed-width 74px thumbs, not percentage-based, so the row's own height is a small, predictable constant regardless of viewport width or story count) -- a further, deliberate reclaim of vertical space, not just a side effect. Verified via a new Playwright suite (real openHome() calls, real CreatorProjectStore.upsert() seeding -- an earlier attempt writing the legacy localStorage key directly was corrected once it became clear Cloud-Primary Project Storage's own in-memory cache mirror only migrates that key once, at boot, so writing it afterward is invisible to the real running app) across 6 viewport sizes (700x650 through 1920x1080): cards now render from 164px up to a genuine 380px (vs. the prior sprint's flat 240px ceiling), zero vertical overflow at every size, the stories strip correctly stays non-scrollable when its content fits and correctly becomes horizontally scrollable once more stories are seeded than fit at a given width. Screenshots confirm the redesigned header row, the reveal-gated Back face still correctly blurred behind Tap to Reveal, and a clean, well-composed layout at both a wide desktop size and a narrow 500px width (header content still fits on one line, story strip visibly scrollable). Full regression: both goldenBuild.js suites pass unchanged (this touches only root Studio CSS/JS). No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to css/style.css and js/magicCardUI.js.
